newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin leaves hospital for government rest home.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin leaves hospital for government rest home.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin left hospital on Friday for a government rest home just outside Moscow where he is expected to spend several weeks continuing his convalescence from open heart surgery.
NTV television showed a smiling president, wearing a fur hat and long dark coat, entering his black Mercedes-Benz limousine.
Reporters at the scene said they saw Yeltsin's motorcade leave the capital's Central Clinical Hospital about 9.15 am (0615 GMT) and head towards the nearby Barvikha sanitorium.
Yeltsin, 65, is said to be making steady progress after his November 5 quintuple bypass operation but doctors have warned him against taking things too fast.
On Wednesday, in his first public appearance since before his operation, Yeltsin said that he was in fighting mood and would return to work after a spell in Barvikha.
He was shown walking slowly and stiffly, but he spoke in a firm voice and there was colour in his cheeks.

The presidential press service said Yeltsin would probably spend two or three weeks at Barvikha, a complex including a sanatorium and government residences near Moscow. Aides say Yeltsin will return to the Kremlin by the end of the year.
Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov is scheduled to brief reporters at 2.30 p.m. (1130 GMT) and presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky is due to brief the media at 11 a.m. (0800 GMT).
